pull.title: test: harden arbitrary-parent block creation
pull.body:
**Problem:** While reviewing #35847, we found that test helpers attaching active-tip block templates to arbitrary parents could retain the wrong work target or subsidy. Rebuilding the coinbase input script for heights 1 through 16 without padding also produces a script below the minimum length. Existing callers avoid these cases or handle them locally, so no current test fails.

**Fix:** Share the parent-dependent reconstruction between `BuildChain()` and `MinerTestingSetup::Block()`. Use the caller-selected timestamp, recalculate the work target and subsidy for the actual parent and height, and append a dummy `OP_0` to the coinbase input script. Require coinbase-only templates so replacing the reward cannot discard transaction fees.

test: derive fork difficulty from parent

`BuildChain` copies the work target from an active-tip template before attaching the block to its requested parent. Recalculate `nBits` from that parent and the rebuilt header so the target describes the resulting child.

A direct helper test uses a different parent target and checks both sides of regtest's min-difficulty delay. Current chain-building callers use regtest with retargeting disabled, so this prevents future invalid test cases rather than fixing an existing failure.

test: derive fork subsidy from parent

`BuildChain` and `validation_block_tests::MinerTestingSetup::Block` attach active-tip templates to arbitrary parents. Derive the child height and subsidy from the actual parent so their coinbases pay the correct subsidy.

`MinerTestingSetup::Block` passes its monotonic timestamp into the reconstruction before customizing the coinbase outputs. Request a coinbase-only template and assert that precondition in the shared helper. Mempool use is enabled by default. Today's calls have an empty mempool, but without these guards a future template could carry transactions while reconstruction replaces its fee-inclusive coinbase reward with the subsidy alone.

Current callers do not cross a subsidy halving, so this prevents future invalid test cases rather than fixing an existing failure.

test: pad low-height fork coinbases

`RebuildBlockForParent` replaces the template coinbase input script with the child height, which encodes to one byte at heights 1 through 16. Append a dummy `OP_0` and remove the validation helper's duplicate padding.

A fork test from genesis through the first subsidy halving checks the rebuilt coinbase and connects every block. The same low-height fork could not pass before the padding change.

Co-authored-by: JP <jeanpablo.jp@hotmail.com>

events.body:
Rebased to resolve conflicts and applied the review suggestions.
The block’s difficulty now uses its actual parent and timestamp, and its coinbase pays the subsidy for its resulting height.
I also added focused tests for the target and coinbase fields through the first halving.

comments.body:
This is an assignment rather than an adjustment, so the template's fees go with it. `MinerTestingSetup::Block` asks for its template with the mempool on, and with one transaction in it the coinbase reward comes out at 5000001000 on master and 5000000000 here, with the block still carrying that transaction.

Nothing hits it today, since the mempool is empty at every call. Would `.use_mempool = false` on that template call be simpler? It makes the site match `BuildChain`, so the overwrite is exact, and the three suites stay green with it.
Sure, added `.use_mempool = false` to `MinerTestingSetup::Block()` and asserted the shared helper receives a coinbase-only block.
Thanks! I added similar tests, with the coinbase cases combined into one fork test. I also credited you as a co-author on the commits containing them.
